item.title: Trump's acknowledgment of Hezbollah 'utterly humiliating' for Netanyahu
item.description: Israel continued to strike southern Lebanon on Tuesday as Iran-backed Hezbollah attacked its troops there despite an apparent Washington-brokered de-escalation deal and a fourth round of US-hosted talks between Lebanon and Israel. FRANCE 24's Jerusalem correspondent Noga Tarnopolsky explains that "on the Israeli side we have simply no acknowledgment of this deal", adding that seeing Trump acknowledge Hezbollah "has been an utter humiliation" for Benjamin Netanyahu.

item.title: Middle East live: Israeli strikes kill eight in Lebanon as Hezbollah rejects latest ceasefire
item.description: Israeli strikes in eastern Lebanon and near the southern city of Tyre killed eight people, the Lebanese health ministry said Thursday as the Israeli army said one of its soldiers was killed combat. Hezbollah earlier rejected a US-backed ceasefire plan agreed by the Lebanese and Israeli governments, demanding that Israel withdraw its troops from southern Lebanon. Follow our liveblog for all the latest.

item.title: Hezbollah Rejects Cease-Fire Deal Between Lebanon and Israel
item.description: Hezbollah’s leader said the Iran-backed group, which was not included in U.S.-brokered talks, said a truce worked out between Israel and the Lebanese government amounted to surrender for his group.

item.title: 'Palestinians are unbelievable people: Vast majority of in Gaza just want to live a normal life'
item.description: Angela Diffley is pleased to welcome Dr. Adi Nadimpalli, Medical Coordinator for Gaza with Doctors Without Borders. He offers a stark assessment of conditions in Gaza following the October 2025 ceasefire. item.title: As Hezbollah rejects truce, families on Israel's northern border describe life under fire
item.description: Residents of Israel's northern border describe life under what they call "the ceasefire war," with sirens and explosions despite agreements.

item.title: Hezbollah chief rejects truce as Israel vows continued operations in south Lebanon
item.description: Hezbollah on Thursday rejected the latest ceasefire agreement between Israel and the Lebanese government, demanding a complete Israeli withdrawal from Lebanon as more fighting there hampered efforts to end the Iran war. The Hezbollah announcement came as Israeli strikes killed at least eight people, according to Lebanese authorities, and a UN peacekeeper was killed in the crossfire.

item.title: Israel strikes hospital in southern Lebanon
item.description: Israel continues to hit targets in Lebanon despite a partial US-brokered ceasefire in place. Lebanese and Israeli diplomats are in Washington for the fourth round of direct talks, but those negotiations have been strongly opposed by Hezbollah. Pressure also mounting within Netanyahu's own government to continue the war in Lebanon.

item.title: Hezbollah denounces Israel-Lebanon ceasefire deal as a ‘farce’
item.description: “We have given no commitment to anyone,” the Iranian-backed militant group's leader said after Israel and Lebanon announced a new U.S.-mediated agreement.

item.title: A 'ceasefire war' in Lebanon continues as 'chaotic global leadership' takes its toll
item.description: Hezbollah's chief on Thursday rejected a conditional truce announced by Lebanese and Israeli envoys, demanding instead a comprehensive ceasefire and full Israeli withdrawal as he threatened northern Israel with new attacks. FRANCE 24's Noga Tarnopolsky reports from Jerusalem.

item.title: Zelensky Mixes Taunts and Peace Talks Offer in Letter to Putin
item.description: “After 26 years in power, age is beginning to take its toll,” President Volodymyr Zelensky of Ukraine wrote of his Russian counterpart, bragging of a recent strike on St. Petersburg.
